thread_analysis.thread_summary: Sony TV (SEC) Bluetooth SIG registration thread for a product with A2DP, AVRCP, and DI. The product is an OS version update of a previously registered TV. The thread covers the full project lifecycle from RFQ to registration completion, with rich Q&A on technical topics: RF test report reuse for OS-update re-registrations, QDID Subset DN selection to avoid inter-layer ICS inconsistencies, mixed PTS version test reports, PTS report file format requirements (Generate Report vs. raw log), 'Design available for other Members to use' portal setting, Compliance Folder timing and document requirements, ICS modification during testing (removing a test case by setting a feature to NO), and Test Case Category D handling.
all_questions_found: We are re-registering for an OS update. The wireless module is unchanged. Can we reuse the RF/RF PHY test reports?
The originally planned Controller QDID creates inter-layer ICS inconsistencies requiring hundreds of additional tests. How do we avoid this?
One test case passes in an older PTS version but fails in the newer one due to a suspected PTS bug. Can we submit reports from two different PTS versions?
We submitted a raw test log file (TestReport_*.zip) as qualification evidence. Why was it rejected?
What does 'Design available for other Members to use' = No mean exactly? Can our own Sony members still reference the design?
Compliance Folder documents — when are they required, and is the TV's block diagram necessary or can we use the module's?
During testing, we discovered the TV software doesn't issue Suspend commands. Can we remove the A2DP Suspend test case?
A test case result is INCONCLUSIVE and Category D. Does it need to pass?

After Submission, we realized we failed to remove an unnecessary Traditional Profile in Layer Selection - is there a faster fix than filing a formal Product Qualification Correction Request Form with SIG Support?
thread_analysis.key_technical_discussion: RF test report reuse: valid when wireless module and RF ICS are identical between old and new registrations. QDID Subset selection: a Subset DN with matching RF power class eliminates inter-layer inconsistencies without additional testing; must compare at LL/RFPHY junction specifically. Mixed PTS versions: SIG accepts test reports from different PTS versions in the same submission as long as all required test cases are covered. PTS report format: 'Generate Report' output (Report_*.xml) is required; raw TestReport_*.zip logs are not accepted. Design sharing: 'No' blocks external SIG members from including the design, but same-company members remain unaffected. Compliance Folder timing: not required before SIG submission — 'promptly after' registration. Block diagram: product is preferred, but wireless module diagram is acceptable for TV (too complex otherwise). ICS modification during testing: A2DP Suspend (ICS 2/8 YES → NO) removes the corresponding test case from scope; this is allowed and reflects the actual product capability. Category D test cases: not required for certification; INCONCLUSIVE result for a Category D case is acceptable.
thread_analysis.key_decision_logic: QDID Subset selection should be done before registration by checking power class matching. PTS version selection should favor stable over latest. ICS modifications during testing must reflect actual product capabilities. All Compliance Folder documents are product-level, not module-level, but practical substitutions are acceptable for complex products like TVs.
thread_analysis.risk_if_done_wrong: Selecting the wrong Controller QDID (creating inter-layer inconsistency) triggers hundreds of additional test items — the most expensive mistake at the pre-registration stage. Submitting raw PTS logs instead of generated reports blocks SIG submission. Using the newest PTS version uncritically risks PTS tool bugs causing false failures.
thread_analysis.consulting_mistake: None identified. The consultant (Sakai) proactively identified the QDID inconsistency problem, found the correct Subset DN solution, and guided Sony through every technical issue in the thread. The thread is a model of thorough pre-registration analysis.
thread_analysis.consulting_takeaway: Pre-registration QDID validation (checking cross-layer consistency before committing) is the highest-value preventive step in the registration process. Always do it. For TV and complex product registrations, always clarify Compliance Folder document granularity (module vs. product level) upfront to prevent late-stage confusion. Educate customers on the PTS Generate Report function before they run any test sessions.
